questions.question: Which of the following was the first major and decisive victory for the East India Company on the soil of India?
questions.solution:
• The Battle of Plassey (1757) was the first major and decisive victory for the East India Company in India.
  • It was fought between Robert Clive of the British East India Company and Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Bengal with his French allies.

questions.question: Which of the following Anglo-Maratha wars resulted in merging the Peshwas' territories with the Bombay Presidency?
questions.solution:
• The Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-1819) resulted in merging the Peshwas' territories with the Bombay Presidency.
  • First Anglo-Maratha War (1775-1782): Marathas won.
  • Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803-1805): British won.

questions.question: Mir Qasim name is associated with which of the following battles of India?
questions.solution:
• Mir Qasim is associated with the Battle of Buxar (1764).
  • The battle was fought between the British East India Company (led by Hector Munro) and the combined army of Shuja-ud-Daulah, Shah Alam II, and Mir Qasim.
  • The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) was signed after this battle.

questions.question: The second Anglo-Mysore War came to an end by signing which of the following treaties?
questions.solution:
• The Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780-84) ended with the Treaty of Mangalore (1784).
  • First Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69): Treaty of Madras.
  • Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92): Treaty of Seringapatam.
  • Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1798-99): Tipu Sultan died.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Karnal (1739):
Statement 1: The Battle of Karnal was fought between Ahmad Shah Abdali and Bahadur Shah I.
Statement 2: After the battle, Ahmad Shah Abdali took the Koh-i-Noor diamond and the Peacock throne to Afghanistan.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct
questions.solution:
• Both statements are incorrect.
  • The Battle of Karnal (1739) was fought between Nadir Shah (not Ahmad Shah Abdali) and the Mughal ruler Muhammad Shah.
  • Nadir Shah looted Delhi and took the Koh-i-Noor diamond and the Peacock throne to Persia, not Afghanistan.

questions.question: Who was the Mughal emperor during the third battle of Panipat?
questions.solution:
• Shah Alam II (Ali Gauhar) was the Mughal emperor during the Third Battle of Panipat (14 January 1761).
  • The battle was fought between the Maratha Empire and Ahmad Shah Abdali. Ahmad Shah Abdali emerged victorious.

questions.question: The Battle of Khatoli was fought in 1517 between the kingdom of Mewar under Rana Sanga and ______.
questions.solution:
• The Battle of Khatoli (1517) was fought between Rana Sanga of Mewar and Ibrahim Lodi.
  • The Lodi dynasty (1451-1526) was the fifth and final dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about historical battles in India:
Statement 1: The Battle of Aliwal (1846) was fought between the British and Sikh forces, without Mughal involvement.
Statement 2: The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought only between the Marathas and the Afghans, with no role of the Mughal army.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: The Battle of Aliwal (1846) was fought during the First Anglo-Sikh War between the British and Sikh forces without Mughal role.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Battle of Buxar (1764) involved the English East India Company against Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula, and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II.

questions.question:
Which of the given statements is correct?
I. When Alivardi Khan died in 1756, Siraj-ud-daulah became the nawab of Bengal.
II. In 1757, Robert Clive led the company's army against Siraj-ud-daulah at Plassey.
questions.solution:
• Both statements are correct.
  • The Battle of Plassey (23 June 1757) was fought between Siraj-ud-Daulah (last independent Nawab of Bengal) and the British East India Company led by Robert Clive (first British Governor of the Bengal Presidency).

questions.question: In which year did Tipu Sultan die defending his capital Seringapatam?
questions.solution:
• Tipu Sultan died in 1799 defending his capital Seringapatam.
  • He is known as the 'Tiger of Mysore'.
  • He was inspired by the ideals of the French Revolution.
  • Daria Daulat Bagh is known as Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace.
  • He was finally defeated by Lord Wellesley.

questions.question: Who emerged victorious in 'The Siege of Arcot' in 1751 AD?
questions.solution:
• The British emerged victorious in the Siege of Arcot (1751 AD).
  • It was fought between the British and combined forces of the French and the Nawab of Arcot.
  • Robert Clive captured Arcot after the battle.
  • The war ended with the Treaty of Pondicherry in 1754.

questions.question: In which year was the Treaty of Versailles signed?
questions.solution:
• The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919.
  • Defeated Germany signed it after the First World War.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Treaty of Yandabo (1826):
Statement 1: The Treaty of Yandabo was signed after the Second Anglo-Maratha War and resulted in the annexation of Odisha by the British.
Statement 2: The Treaty of Yandabo was signed between the British and Burmese after the First Anglo-Burmese War in 1826.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: The Treaty of Yandabo was unrelated to the Anglo-Maratha War or Odisha's annexation.
  • Statement 2 is correct: It was signed in 1826 after the First Anglo-Burmese War, ceding Assam, Manipur, Arakan, and Tenasserim to the British.

questions.question: In 1818, the Holkar Dynasty signed the Treaty of Mandsaur with the _____.
questions.solution:
• The Holkar Dynasty signed the Treaty of Mandsaur with the British in 1818.
  • After Malhar Rao II was defeated in the Battle of Mahidpur (1817), the treaty was signed.

questions.question: Which of the following battles did Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah fight, defeating the forces under Henry Lawrence?
questions.solution:
• Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah fought and defeated Henry Lawrence's forces in the Battle of Chinhat.
  • The Battle of Chinhat was fought on the morning of 30 June 1857 between British forces and Indian rebels.
  • Barkat Ahmad was declared Chief Army Officer of the rebels in this battle.

questions.question: In the Battle of Swally (1612) the British fought against the
questions.solution:
• In the Battle of Swally (1612), the British fought against the Portuguese.
  • The battle took place on 29-30 November 1612 off the coast of Suvali, a village near Surat city.
  • It marked the beginning of the end of Portugal's commercial monopoly over India.

questions.question: The Battle of Bedara was fought between the British Army and the Dutch Army in:
questions.solution:
• The Battle of Bedara was fought on 25 November 1759 during the Seven Years' War.
  • It was fought between a force of British troops of the British East India Company and a force of the Dutch East India Company.

questions.question: The British annexed Punjab after defeating the Sikhs in the Anglo-Sikh War in the year
questions.solution:
• The British annexed Punjab in 1849 after defeating the Sikhs in the Anglo-Sikh War.
  • This war resulted in the fall of the Sikh Empire, and Punjab became part of the North West Frontier Province.

questions.question: Who signed the treaty of Alinagar with the British?
questions.solution:
• Siraj-ud-Daula signed the Treaty of Alinagar with the British on 9 February 1757.
  • It was signed between Robert Clive of the British East India Company and the Nawab of Bengal, Mirza Muhammad Siraj Ud Daula.
  • The Nawab would recognize all provisions of Mughal Emperor Farrukhsiyar's farman of 1717.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the regional features of Gujarat's medieval architecture?
1. Architectural forms in Gujarat often incorporated elements from local temple traditions.
2. Structures such as mosques and tombs in Gujarat featured ornamental carvings like toranas and bell motifs.
3. Gujarat's architectural style strictly avoided any decorative influence from indigenous practices.
questions.solution:
• Statements 1 and 2 are correct.
  • Gujarat's medieval architecture represents Indo-Islamic fusion, with local Hindu and Jain craftsmen applying temple-building skills to mosques.
  • Ornamental carvings like toranas, lotus motifs, chain-and-bell designs, and floral patterns were used.
  • Statement 3 is incorrect because the style incorporated indigenous practices.

questions.question:
Given below are assertion and reason, read the statements and choose the correct option.
Assertion: (A) British capital accumulation in the 18th century was reinvested in industrial development.
Reason: (R) The capital was largely controlled by merchants and industrialists instead of the feudal aristocracy.
questions.option_1: A is true, but R is false.
questions.option_2: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true.
questions.solution:
• Both Assertion and Reason are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
  • In 18th-century Britain, capital from the Agricultural Revolution, overseas trade, slave trade, and colonial profits was reinvested in factories, technologies, and infrastructure.
  • Merchants and industrialists (not feudal aristocracy) actively took risks in commerce and industry, driving economic transformation.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Trinity of Carnatic Music and choose the correct option:
Statement 1: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Shyama Shastri lived during the 17th century.
Statement 2: The trinity elevated the kriti to a higher musical form.
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: The Trinity of Carnatic Music lived during the 18th century, not the 17th.
  • Statement 2 is correct: They elevated the kriti to a higher musical form.
  • The Trinity consists of Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri.

questions.question:
Match the following cave sites with their architectural characteristics:
A. Udayagiri → 1. Circular chaitya with stupa and arch
B. Guntapalle → 2. Pillared veranda with cells at the back
C. Khandagiri → 3. Animal-shaped single rock excavations
questions.solution:
• The correct matching is:
    • Udayagiri - Pillared veranda with cells at the back (monastic dwellings)
    • Guntapalle - Circular chaitya with stupa and arch (ritualistic architecture)
    • Khandagiri - Animal-shaped single rock excavations (sculptural creativity)

questions.question: Which feature is not commonly associated with French colonial architecture in India?
questions.solution:
• Ornate Mughal domes are not associated with French colonial architecture in India.
  • French colonial features: wide verandas (ventilation and shade), tall doors and windows (cross-ventilation), sloped tiled roofs (monsoon rains), pastel colors, courtyards, symmetry.
  • Ornate Mughal domes are a feature of Mughal architecture (e.g., Taj Mahal, Humayun's Tomb).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding temple architecture in India:
1. The Dravidian style of temple architecture flourished mainly in Northern India.
2. The Vesara style represents a fusion of Nagara and Dravida styles.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: Dravidian style flourished mainly in Southern India, not Northern India.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Vesara style is indeed a blend of Nagara and Dravida with a bell-shaped tower.
